executiveSummary:
Client Documentation Hub is a secure, AI-assisted client-facing documentation portal hosted at docs.wsd.com that automatically publishes approved Confluence pages to the right clients. Internal teams continue to author in Confluence as the single source of truth; the Hub mirrors approved, tagged pages in near real-time, enforces per-client access, retains a version history, and uses AI to (a) screen content for sensitive data before publishing, (b) generate release notes and per-client change summaries, and (c) email clients when their documentation changes. The Hub replaces today's manual PDF export plus email distribution and the unscalable Confluence guest-access pattern.

Today WSD authors documentation in Confluence but delivers it to clients as PDFs. Every release the docs team exports new PDFs, emails them to a contact list, and chases which version each client is reading. Confluence guest access and per-client Confluence spaces have been tried and do not scale (license cost, space sprawl, permission drift, no audit trail). The cost is concrete: support tickets against stale PDFs, hours of manual distribution per release, no auditable record of who read which version, and a split source of truth between Confluence and the latest emailed PDF.

The MVP delivers three layers in parallel: a Confluence-driven publishing pipeline (label / approval-gated, near real-time sync, immutable version history); a multi-tenant client portal with secure authentication, per-client and shared visibility, browse/search/version-history/PDF-download, and notifications; and an AI layer that screens pages for secrets and internal references before publish, generates release notes / change summaries / notification emails, and scores documentation quality. Phase 3 capabilities (in-portal AI assistant, analytics, client-impact analysis) are explicitly out of scope.

The portal targets WSD client engineers, integrators, and operators as the primary readers, WSD documentation owners as authors, and WSD release reviewers as the human gate over AI output. Success means: ≥95% reduction in manual PDF distribution, p95 sync latency under 5 minutes, ≥90% of AI-screened pages clearing first-pass review, and zero unauthorised cross-client document accesses on the audit log.
problemStatement: WSD authors documentation in Confluence but delivers it to clients as PDFs that are exported, emailed, and version-chased manually for every release. Guest Confluence access and per-client Confluence spaces have been tried and do not scale, producing stale PDFs in client hands, hours of manual distribution work per release, no auditable record of who saw which version, and a split source of truth between Confluence and the latest emailed PDF.
targetUsers: Client end users (engineers, integrators, operators at WSD client companies) who read product, API, and integration documentation
WSD documentation owners who author and tag pages in Confluence and approve them for publication
WSD release and publishing reviewers who approve AI screening results and AI-generated release notes before they reach clients
Client admins who manage which of their team members can access the client's portal account
WSD security and compliance staff who consume audit logs to demonstrate access control and content review
inScope: Selective sync of approved Confluence pages via configurable label / tag and space allow-list
Approval-state gating: only pages flagged as approved in Confluence are eligible for publication
Near real-time publishing with p95 end-to-end latency under 5 minutes from approval to portal visibility
Immutable per-page version history with at least the last 20 versions retained
Manual sync re-trigger and unpublish actions for doc owners, audit-logged
Secure multi-tenant authentication with password + second factor, optional SAML 2.0 / OIDC SSO
Per-client access scoping with shared and client-specific document visibility
Client-admin role for tenant-level user lifecycle (invite, disable, remove)
Audit log of authentication, document views, and admin actions, retained ≥ 12 months
Browsable portal organised by product and guide category derived from Confluence labels
Per-page version history view with diff against latest
Per-page on-demand PDF generation of any version
Full-text search scoped to the user's entitled documents
Per-user 'last visited' tracking driving AI change-summary feature
Email notifications on documentation changes with configurable cadence (immediate / daily / weekly)
Pre-publish AI document review screening for secrets, internal URLs, Jira links, internal emails, and structurally missing content
Hard block on high-severity AI findings until reviewer confirms false positive or page is corrected
AI-authored release notes (What's New / Breaking Changes / Recommended Actions) with reviewer approval gate
Per-client 'Since your last visit' AI change summary on the portal landing page
AI-generated client notification email summaries, reviewer-approved when breaking
AI documentation quality scoring (completeness / readability / missing examples / missing API responses) as soft warnings
Responsive web portal accessible on modern desktop and tablet browsers
outOfScope: Replacing Confluence as the authoring tool
Two-way sync; portal content is read-only relative to Confluence
In-portal AI chat assistant ('ask the docs') — Phase 3
Per-client usage analytics dashboards and client-impact analysis — Phase 3
Authoring or editing documentation from inside the portal
Multilingual translation of documentation; English-only first release
Migration of historical PDF artefacts into the portal's version history
Integration with non-Confluence content sources (Notion, Google Docs, GitHub markdown) for first release
Quality-score trend dashboards beyond a per-page warning surface in v1
objectives: Reduce manual PDF distribution emails sent by the docs team by ≥ 95% within 90 days of launch
Achieve p95 sync latency under 5 minutes from Confluence approval to portal visibility (max under 15 minutes including AI review)
Have ≥ 90% of AI-screened pages clear review on first pass with zero sensitive-content false negatives reaching clients
Drive ≥ 60% of subscribed clients to open at least one AI change-summary email per release cycle within 90 days
Maintain zero unauthorised cross-client document accesses in the security audit
Reduce documentation-related support tickets attributable to stale version or missing PDF by ≥ 70% in 90 days
Keep Confluence as the single source of truth — no parallel authoring surface introduced
Establish auditable access and content-review records that satisfy security and compliance review without manual collation
constraints: Authoring continues in the existing WSD Confluence instance; no change to the writer workflow beyond adopting the documented label / approval conventions
Confluence REST API access (read + change-event subscription) is available to the sync service
An approved AI provider (Claude on Anthropic API or via Bedrock; final choice in TAD) is used for review, release-notes, summary, and notification generation; provider keys are managed by platform
Email delivery is via an existing transactional email provider (SES / SendGrid); the Hub does not run its own MTA
Hosted under docs.wsd.com on the standard WSD container platform; specific platform choice deferred to TAD
Initial client tenant provisioning is operator-driven (WSD provisions the tenant); client-admin self-service is only for end-user lifecycle, not tenant creation
AI document-review pipeline must fail closed: unavailable AI provider means pages remain unpublished, never bypassed
All client data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher; auth tokens, session cookies, and AI-pipeline payloads must be encrypted at rest
Portal must meet WCAG 2.1 AA for primary client-facing reading and navigation flows
Tamper-evident audit logging (append-only or signed) retained ≥ 12 months

glossary.Confluence: WSD's existing wiki / documentation authoring platform; the source of truth for all documentation content.
glossary.Hub / Client Documentation Hub: The new client-facing portal at docs.wsd.com that publishes approved Confluence pages to clients.
glossary.Tenant: An isolated logical workspace within the Hub representing one client company, with its own users and document scope.
glossary.Shared document: A document visible to all authenticated client tenants (e.g. general product documentation).
glossary.Client-specific document: A document visible only to one or more named client tenants (e.g. client-specific runbooks).
glossary.Publish: The act of pushing an approved Confluence page version through AI review and into the portal as the latest version.
glossary.Approval signal: The configurable Confluence indicator (label, page status, or workflow state) that marks a page as ready to publish.
glossary.AI document review: Pre-publish AI screening pass for secrets, internal URLs, Jira links, internal emails, and missing content.
glossary.Change summary: An AI-generated per-client 'Since your last visit' summary surfaced on the portal landing page.
glossary.Release notes: AI-generated What's New / Breaking Changes / Recommended Actions for a changed page, gated by reviewer approval.
glossary.Fail closed: Behaviour where, on AI-provider failure, the system blocks publishing rather than allowing pages through unscreened.
glossary.WCAG 2.1 AA: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.1, conformance level AA — the accessibility target for the portal.

requirements.title: Selective Confluence sync via tag / space allow-list
requirements.description: The system shall sync Confluence pages to the portal selectively, driven by a configurable allow-list of Confluence labels / tags and source spaces, so that only intentionally-tagged pages are eligible for publication. The allow-list shall be maintained by a documentation administrator and changes shall take effect on the next sync cycle without requiring a deploy.
requirements.rationale: WSD's Confluence instance contains many pages that must never reach clients (internal runbooks, drafts, HR content). An explicit allow-list keeps the publishing surface intentional and small and prevents accidental over-sharing.

requirements.title: Approval-state gating
requirements.description: The system shall only publish pages that are in an 'approved' state, determined by a configurable approval signal in Confluence (label, page status, or workflow state), and shall reject draft / in-review pages from publishing. Pages that lose their approval state after publish shall be unpublished on the next sync.
requirements.rationale: Clients must never see unfinished or unreviewed content. Explicit approval gating turns publish into a deliberate act rather than a side effect of editing.

requirements.title: Near real-time publishing
requirements.description: The system shall detect Confluence page changes and publish updates to the portal in near real-time, with p95 end-to-end latency under 5 minutes from approval to portal visibility. The sync mechanism shall use Confluence change events (webhooks) where available and fall back to polling on a configurable interval.
requirements.rationale: Manual PDF distribution today takes hours to days. The portal must close that gap to make Confluence the obvious place to update something that clients should see.

requirements.title: Per-page version history
requirements.description: The system shall maintain a version history for every published page, retaining at minimum the last 20 versions per page, each with its publish timestamp, source Confluence version ID, and the publisher's identity. Versions shall be immutable once published.
requirements.rationale: Clients often integrate against a specific documented version and need to refer back to it; security needs to prove what was published when.

requirements.title: Preserve Confluence page structure on publish
requirements.description: The system shall preserve Confluence page structure on publish: headings, lists, tables, code blocks, inline images, and internal cross-links between published pages. Cross-links to non-published pages shall be rewritten to a clear 'not available' state rather than broken or leaking to Confluence.
requirements.rationale: Doc owners author rich pages in Confluence; if the portal renders a flattened version, they will work around the portal and clients lose the canonical experience.

requirements.title: Manual sync re-trigger
requirements.description: The system shall allow a documentation owner to manually re-trigger sync of an individual page or a tag set from an admin UI when an automatic sync is suspected to have been missed, with the action audit-logged.
requirements.rationale: Even with webhooks and polling, edge cases miss events. A manual button beats opening a support ticket against the platform team.

requirements.title: Unpublish without deleting from Confluence
requirements.description: The system shall support unpublishing a page (removal from the portal) without deleting it from Confluence, with an audit-logged reason supplied by the operator. An unpublished page remains in the version history but is not reachable from the portal browse / search.
requirements.rationale: Mistakes happen and need a fast remediation path that does not destroy authoring history.

requirements.title: Authentication required for all portal pages
requirements.description: The system shall require authenticated login for every portal page; no documentation content shall be reachable unauthenticated. Unauthenticated requests shall be redirected to the login flow, preserving the intended destination.
requirements.rationale: The Hub exists precisely because guest Confluence access leaked content. The whole portal is gated.

requirements.title: Secure login with second factor
requirements.description: The system shall support a secure login flow with password + second factor (TOTP or email magic link), with industry-standard session handling: HTTP-only Secure cookies, CSRF protection, idempotent logout, configurable session timeout, and brute-force protection (account lockout / rate limiting).
requirements.rationale: Documentation may contain sensitive integration details and client-specific commercial content; single-factor login is not acceptable.

requirements.title: Per-client access scoping
requirements.description: The system shall enforce per-client access scoping: a logged-in user belongs to one client tenant, and the portal shall only render documents marked as shared or as scoped to that client. Access scoping is enforced at the data-access layer, not only in the UI.
requirements.rationale: Cross-client data leakage is the highest-severity failure mode of a multi-tenant client portal; UI-only enforcement is insufficient.

requirements.title: Shared vs client-specific document visibility
requirements.description: The system shall support two document visibility scopes: 'shared' (visible to all authenticated clients) and 'client-specific' (visible only to the named client(s)), with scope set per Confluence page via a label or page property as defined by the publish convention.
requirements.rationale: Most documentation is shared; some (runbooks, integration secrets, commercial annexes) is client-bound. The model must support both with no second sync surface.

requirements.title: Client-admin role for tenant user lifecycle
requirements.description: The system shall provide a client-admin role allowing a designated client contact to invite, disable, and remove users within their own client tenant without WSD intervention. Client-admin actions are scoped to the admin's own tenant and audit-logged.
requirements.rationale: If WSD operators must provision every client user, onboarding latency negates the portal's value.

requirements.title: Enterprise SSO via SAML / OIDC
requirements.description: The system shall support SSO via SAML 2.0 or OIDC for client tenants that require enterprise login. SSO configuration is per tenant and, when enabled, replaces password + second factor for that tenant's users.
requirements.rationale: Enterprise clients commonly mandate SSO. Going without SSO blocks some named launch clients but not all of them.

requirements.title: Audit log of auth, view, and admin actions
requirements.description: The system shall maintain an audit log of every authentication event (success / failure / lockout), every document view, and every administrative action (invite, role change, scope change, unpublish, sync re-trigger, AI review decision), retained for at least 12 months.
requirements.rationale: Security must be able to answer 'who saw page X version Y on date Z' from a single source; today they cannot.

requirements.title: Browse navigation by product and guide category
requirements.description: The portal shall present a browsable navigation grouped by product and guide category, derived from the source Confluence label / page hierarchy. The grouping shall be deterministic for the same set of labels so reviewers can predict where a page will appear.
requirements.rationale: Clients integrate with multiple products; flat lists do not scale beyond a handful of pages.

requirements.title: Latest version is the default view
requirements.description: The portal shall render the latest published version of a page as the default view, with the page's last-updated timestamp visible and a clear visual indicator that this is the current version.
requirements.rationale: The whole point of the portal is that 'latest' is the default; the user must never have to guess.

requirements.title: Version history view with diff
requirements.description: The portal shall expose a per-page version history view, allowing the user to read any previous published version and to diff it against the latest. The diff shall highlight added, removed, and changed content at the block level.
requirements.rationale: Clients pinned to an older integration need to see what changed between versions to plan upgrades.

requirements.title: Per-page PDF download
requirements.description: The portal shall provide a per-page 'Download as PDF' action that generates a styled PDF of the currently-viewed version on demand. The PDF shall include the document title, version, timestamp, and client identity in a footer for audit.
requirements.rationale: Many clients still want a PDF for offline reading or internal distribution; on-demand PDF preserves that workflow without the manual-export burden.

requirements.title: Scoped full-text search
requirements.description: The portal shall provide full-text search scoped to the documents the logged-in user is permitted to see, with results ranked by relevance and filterable by product. Search results that would expose document titles a user is not entitled to see shall be excluded.
requirements.rationale: Browse navigation is not enough at scale; search is how integrators find what they need.

requirements.title: Per-user 'last visited' tracking
requirements.description: The portal shall remember a per-user 'last visited' timestamp per page so that the AI change-summary feature can show 'what's new since you last looked'. Tracking is per user, not per tenant, and is treated as personal data subject to the same retention policy.
requirements.rationale: Without 'since your last visit', the AI change summary degrades to a generic recent-changes feed.

requirements.title: Email notifications on documentation changes
requirements.description: The system shall notify subscribed client users by email when documentation they are entitled to see has changed since the last digest, with a configurable digest cadence per user: immediate, daily, or weekly. Notifications respect the access scope; no user receives an email about a page they cannot read.
requirements.rationale: Clients will not check the portal on a schedule; push is required to make the portal effective.

requirements.title: Release-highlights summary in notification email
requirements.description: Each notification email shall include a release-highlights summary and a deep link into the portal for each changed page. The summary text is produced by the AI client-notification feature (REQ-053); REQ-031 covers the structural email content.
requirements.rationale: Emails without a summary are noise; emails with a summary drive opens and portal visits.

requirements.title: Self-service notification preferences
requirements.description: Client users shall be able to manage their own notification preferences (cadence, per-product subscription, mute) from a profile page without contacting WSD.
requirements.rationale: Forcing every preference change through WSD support negates the self-service value of the portal.

requirements.title: Pre-publish AI document review
requirements.description: Before a page is published, the system shall run an AI document-review pass that flags: secrets / credentials / API keys, internal-only URLs, Jira / internal-ticket links, internal employee email addresses, and structurally missing content (e.g. empty sections, placeholders such as 'TODO', 'TBD', 'lorem ipsum'). The pipeline shall fail closed on AI provider unavailability.
requirements.rationale: The single highest-risk failure of a client portal is leaking a secret; an automated screening pass that the human reviewer cannot forget is the strongest control.

requirements.title: Hard block on high-severity AI findings
requirements.description: A page that triggers any high-severity AI review finding (secrets, internal URLs, Jira links, internal email addresses) shall be blocked from publishing until either a reviewer explicitly confirms a false positive or the page is corrected in Confluence and re-synced. A blocked page shall surface a clear actionable state to the doc owner.
requirements.rationale: If AI findings are advisory only, they will be ignored under deadline pressure; the gate must be hard for high-severity categories.

requirements.title: Reviewer view of AI findings in context
requirements.description: The AI review result shall be shown to the publishing reviewer with the matched span highlighted in context and a per-finding 'ignore / acknowledge / block' action, with all decisions audit-logged including reviewer identity, timestamp, and per-finding choice.
requirements.rationale: An opaque verdict is unworkable; reviewers need to see exactly what triggered each finding to judge it.

requirements.title: AI release notes per page change
requirements.description: When a published page changes, the system shall generate AI-authored release notes for that page covering three sections: What's New, Breaking Changes, and Recommended Actions. The docs team approves before clients see them; release notes do not auto-publish on first generation.
requirements.rationale: Hand-writing release notes per page per release is the largest manual cost today; AI authorship with human approval inverts that ratio.

requirements.title: Per-client 'Since your last visit' summary
requirements.description: On a client's portal landing page, the system shall show a per-client 'Since your last visit' summary, AI-generated from the diff of pages they are entitled to see and have not yet viewed in the latest version. The summary is regenerated on landing-page load when underlying changes have occurred.
requirements.rationale: Clients who return after a gap need a fast orientation; without it they will miss changes that matter.

requirements.title: Reviewer can regenerate, edit, or discard AI release notes
requirements.description: The system shall let a reviewer regenerate, edit inline, or discard any AI-generated release-notes block before it is published. Edits are preserved on subsequent regeneration prompts unless the reviewer explicitly discards them.
requirements.rationale: AI output is a draft, not the final voice; reviewers need fast levers to correct it.

requirements.title: AI-generated client notification email summaries
requirements.description: Notification emails sent under REQ-030 shall use AI-generated concise summaries (e.g. 'Store API updated. New inventory APIs added. No action required.'), generated per client based on the changes they are entitled to see. Summaries flagged as breaking shall be reviewer-approved before send; non-breaking summaries may send automatically.
requirements.rationale: Generic notification emails get ignored; concise per-client summaries drive opens and portal visits.

requirements.title: AI documentation quality scoring
requirements.description: Before publish, the system shall score each page on Completeness, Readability, Missing Examples, and Missing API Responses, surfacing the scores to the doc owner. Low scores produce warnings, not hard blocks; doc owners can publish anyway and the score is recorded in the audit trail.
requirements.rationale: Quality scoring is a nudge, not a gate; making it a hard block would create perverse incentives to write bland passing prose.

requirements.title: Quality-score trend per page
requirements.description: The system shall trend quality scores over time per page so doc owners can see documentation health regressing or improving across publishes.
requirements.rationale: Useful for doc-team retros but not on the critical path for v1 release.

requirements.title: Portal page render p95 under 1.5 s
requirements.description: Portal page render p95 shall be under 1.5 s under expected client load (target: 500 concurrent authenticated users at launch), measured from request receipt to last byte of HTML on a representative documentation page.
requirements.rationale: Reading documentation is a low-tolerance UX; slow pages drive clients back to PDFs.

requirements.title: Sync latency p95 under 5 minutes
requirements.description: End-to-end sync latency p95 from Confluence approval to portal visibility shall be under 5 minutes; maximum (including AI review) shall be under 15 minutes. Sync latency shall be observable via a platform metric.
requirements.rationale: Faster than this is overkill; slower than this and the docs team will start sending updates by email again.

requirements.title: Encryption in transit and at rest
requirements.description: All client data in transit shall use TLS 1.2 or higher; all authentication tokens, session cookies, and AI-pipeline payloads (including draft pages awaiting review) shall be encrypted at rest using platform-standard KMS-managed keys.
requirements.rationale: Industry baseline; non-negotiable for a client portal.

requirements.title: Per-client data isolation at data-access layer
requirements.description: Per-client data isolation shall be enforced at the data-access layer; no portal endpoint may return content scoped to a client other than the requesting user's client, even under URL manipulation, parameter tampering, or direct API access. Tenant isolation shall be validated by automated test on every release.
requirements.rationale: Cross-tenant data leakage is the highest-impact failure mode; defence-in-depth requires enforcement below the UI.

requirements.title: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility for primary client flows
requirements.description: The portal shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA for all primary client-facing reading and navigation flows: login, browse, read, version history, search, PDF download. Compliance is verified by automated accessibility checks plus targeted manual review per release.
requirements.rationale: Client engineers include users who rely on assistive technology; WCAG AA is the WSD platform standard.

requirements.title: AI review pipeline fails closed
requirements.description: The AI document-review pipeline shall fail closed: if an AI provider is unavailable or returns a non-conclusive result, pages remain unpublished and a reviewer is alerted; pages shall not bypass screening regardless of operator pressure.
requirements.rationale: Fail-open behaviour negates the entire AI screening control on the days it matters most.

requirements.title: Horizontal scaling of the portal read tier
requirements.description: The system shall support horizontal scaling of the portal read tier so capacity grows linearly with client headcount with no architectural change. Read-tier nodes shall be stateless and addable / removable behind the load balancer without portal downtime.
requirements.rationale: Onboarding a large client should not trigger a re-architecture.

requirements.title: Tamper-evident audit log retention
requirements.description: Audit logs (authentication, document view, admin actions, AI review decisions, sync re-trigger, unpublish) shall be tamper-evident — append-only or cryptographically signed — and retained for at least 12 months in a separate storage tier with restricted access.
requirements.rationale: If audit logs can be edited by the same operators they record, they are not evidence.
